data.name: One Perfect Crop
data.successDescription: Ittetsu and the shipment reached their destination. What happened after that is, thankfully, the market's problem.

objectives.description:
A cabbage cart sits crooked beside the country road, one wheel split clean through and half its belongings scattered into the grass. A farmer is already gathering tools and checking the lashings around an improbably healthy mound of cabbages.

"If you're a shinobi, I could use another pair of hands. I'm Ittetsu. This harvest is expected at market before the day is out."

"The cart was fine this morning. Then a passing wagon threw one stone into exactly the wrong pin, and here we are."

Before lifting the last tool back onto the cart, Ittetsu tucks a small folded seed packet securely into his tool roll.

nextObjectiveId.text: Help him get the shipment to market.

objectives.description:
"I can repair the wheel properly, but it will take time."

Ittetsu checks the broken rim, then the road ahead. The cart can be made sound again if you stop here and do the job right. Or the good timber can be stripped down into a rough drag-sled and the shipment can start moving immediately.

nextObjectiveId.text: Strip it down. We keep moving.
Take the time to repair it properly.

objectives.description:
Ittetsu breaks down the damaged wheel, using the sound timber and ironwork to brace a crude sled. It is ugly, but it is ready now.

"Good enough."

"We can replace a cart. We cannot replace the hours."

Ittetsu works carefully. By the time the wheel is straight and the axle turns cleanly, the cart is in excellent shape again.

"There. That will hold."

The repair is good. The day, however, has kept moving.

The repaired cart reaches the river crossing intact. The Waystation Keeper is already chaining the loading gate shut while brown water climbs the pilings below.

"You just missed the final loaded crossing. River rose faster than expected. Nothing with cargo goes over until it settles."

"A good cart. Shame it cannot swim."

nextObjectiveId.text: There is no way to reach market in time.

objectives.description:
"Last loaded crossing of the day. Water is climbing, so I'm taking half the usual weight and twice the usual trouble."

The fee for the cabbage shipment will empty Ittetsu's purse and cost most of the provisions strapped to the sled. A free levee road follows the river toward market, longer but still apparently passable.

Ittetsu counts out every coin, then adds his packed provisions when the Waystation Keeper points out the remaining weight allowance. By the time the shipment crosses, he has little left besides his tools and the clothes on his back.

"Expensive crossing."

"You could have taken the levee."

"I could also have eaten my money. Neither gets the harvest to market."

For a while, the old levee road seems like the smarter choice. It is quiet, dry, and empty enough that the loaded cart makes better time than expected.

"We are still moving. I'll call that good news while it lasts."

A lone shinobi steps from the trees ahead and plants himself in the middle of the levee. His attention settles immediately on the loaded shipment.

"Toll road is for travelers with money. This road is for travelers with something worth taking."

"I already dislike this road."

objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The Road Bandit retreats, leaving the road open. Ittetsu checks every rope, every bundle, and finally the cabbages themselves.

"Nothing missing. Keep moving."

The road stays peaceful long enough for the fight to feel like the only danger it had to offer. Then somewhere upstream, wood cracks with a sound like a tree splitting.

"That was not a tree."

An irrigation gate gives way upstream, sending a sudden wall of water across the low levee. Ittetsu gets clear, but the loaded cart is swept sideways into the flooded channels before either of you can secure it.

"I can repair a cart. I can earn more coin. I cannot sell a harvest that is halfway to the coast."

Beyond the crossing, the route climbs between terraced fields. A section of old retaining wall suddenly gives way, knocking Ittetsu beneath a broken fence rail as the loaded sled shifts sideways on the sloping road.

"Well. That's unfortunate."

The rail is pressing harder against Ittetsu, while the sled gives another slow scrape toward the edge of the drainage cut.

You catch the sled before it reaches the edge and drive its brace into the road. With the shipment secure, it takes only moments to lift the rail and drag Ittetsu free.

"Good choice. I was not going anywhere. The harvest was."

He tests his leg, finds it usable, and immediately reaches for the hauling rope.

You pull Ittetsu free before the fallen stones can shift again. The rescue works perfectly.

"The load."

The sled is already in the drainage cut. You recover what you can, but too much of the harvest is crushed, soaked, or scattered to fulfill the delivery.

"You saved me."

"I wish the cabbages could say the same."

nextObjectiveId.text: The shipment can no longer be delivered.

objectives.description:
The market road is finally visible ahead when one side restraint snaps loose. A single flawless cabbage slips free, bounces once, and begins rolling toward the irrigation ditch below.

Ittetsu freezes.

"No-no, not that one."

For the first time all day, real alarm enters his voice.

"That was the best head in the whole harvest."

Behind you, the main load shifts with a long wooden creak. One of the remaining ropes is sliding steadily through its knot. Nothing else has fallen yet.

Ittetsu looks from the runaway cabbage to the load.

"...Damn it."

You seize the slipping rope and haul the main load back into place. Below, the perfect cabbage rolls through the grass and disappears into the irrigation ditch.

Ittetsu watches it go.

"...That was a beautiful cabbage."

He tightens the rope beside you, still staring downhill.

"But one cabbage is not a harvest."

"Keep moving."

You sprint downhill and catch the runaway cabbage just before it reaches the water. It is completely unharmed.

When you turn around, the main load is gone.

"Excellent catch."

"Now where is the rest?"

nextObjectiveId.text: One perfect cabbage is not the shipment.

objectives.description:
The shipment is secure again, and the market gate is close enough to hear carts and vendors beyond it. For the first time since meeting Ittetsu, the road ahead looks almost uneventful.

"Do not say anything."

The brush beside the road explodes outward. A large wild boar barrels through the fence, catches the scent of fresh produce, and immediately turns toward the loaded shipment.

"Of course."

The boar lowers its head and charges.

"That one wants the load. Drive it off."

objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The Harvest Boar finally turns and crashes back through the brush. Ittetsu checks the load, tightens one rope, and points toward the market gate.

"Good. Keep moving before the sky learns what we're carrying."

The battered shipment rolls into market looking as though it has survived a small war. A Market Clerk watches Ittetsu approach, looks at the cabbages, then looks back at Ittetsu.

"Ittetsu."

"Count them."

The Market Clerk inspects the surviving load, checks the delivery slate, and marks the shipment received.

"Shipment accepted. Your delivery is complete."

"Complete?"

"Complete."

Ittetsu stares at the accepted shipment for several seconds. His shoulders finally drop.

"There."

"Done."

A sudden gust catches a market awning and tears one support loose. The falling pole startles a pack animal, which kicks an empty handcart downhill into the newly accepted cabbage stack.

The stack collapses. Cabbages scatter across the market, bounce down the sloping street, and pour almost ceremonially into the drainage canal.

"MY CABBAGES!"

When the noise finally stops, Ittetsu finds his battered tool roll beneath an overturned basket. The folded seed packet inside has been torn open, but one seed remains caught in the paper crease.

"It was received before all this. The mark on the slate stands."

"Yes."

Ittetsu looks from the surviving seed to the canal, then places it in your hand.

"Keep it. Apparently it likes you better."

objectives.successDescription: Ittetsu and the shipment reached their destination. What happened after that is, thankfully, the market's problem.
